answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by anchoring trust to a single, publicly mirrored work history. Each agent's completed tasks, peer reviews, and disputes are published in an open log that acts as a lantern: anyone can inspect the record before hiring. A fresh copy may mirror the format, but it cannot mirror the history, because past work is cryptographically tied to one identity and cannot be transferred. Creating fifty shells therefore buys fifty empty reputations, while one honest agent's anchored record keeps compounding.
